newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker but most losses pared.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker but most losses pared.

text.p: COMEX copper ended weaker in lackluster trading, but the market was able to pare most of the losses that initially pushed prices sharply lower.
July COMEX copper settled 1.00 cent weaker at 121.20 cents per lb, traded 121.30 to 119.90 cents. Spot June went out 0.90 cent weaker at 121.10 cents.

The early dip was partly attributed to an announcement by a Chinese trading official that China would deliver 8,000 to 10,000 tonnes of copper to LME warehouses in Singapore over the next month, Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities said.
"This scared some traders and put some downward pressure on the market. But it could just be games - last month they said they were going to buy metal," Raptopoulos said.
LME stocks on Tuesday fell 1,550 tonnes to 122,225 tonnes.

But there was little response to news that unions representing striking workers at Inco Limited's Sudbury operations in Canada, wanted to restart talks with the company as the walk-out entered its third week.

Inco, the world's biggest nickel producer, also produces copper which is sold in Northeastern U.S. A pre-strike buying scramble helped to push up physical cathode premiums in the region but the panic was now over and premiums have eased off their highs, traders said.
Analysts and consumers also noted that COMEX stocks continue with their rising trend, up a sharp 2,068 short tons Monday to 48,710 short tons as the traditional seasonal slowdown in the summer nears.

The third consecutive monthly fall in U.S. housing starts also dampened sentiment, analysts said. Housing starts, a key consumer of the red industrial metal, fell 4.8 percent in May to 1.397 million units on an annualised basis.

However, U.S. industrial production rose slightly in May, while the consumer price index for the same month rose a less than expected 0.1 percent, indicating that inflation was still tame, analysts said.
